questions.learningObjective: compute log Ksp from molar solubility
questions.stem: In the replicate aliquot transfer exercise below, a technician obtains the reported result. A 1 to 1 ionic solid has a molar solubility of 3.27e-5 M. What is log Ksp for this salt?

options.misconception: confuses the logarithm of solubility with that of the solubility product
reports pS rather than the logarithm of Ksp
uses the exponent appropriate to a two-to-one salt

questions.explanation: For a one-to-one salt each ion has concentration s, so Ksp equals s squared and log Ksp is twice log s. Confusing Ksp with s or borrowing the exponent of a different salt stoichiometry gives the wrong power.
questions.hint: Ksp = s² for a 1:1 salt.

questions.learningObjective: compute log solubility from Ksp
questions.stem: A 1 to 1 salt has Ksp = 1.84e-8. Determine the value of negative log s, where s is the molar solubility in pure water?

options.misconception: uses pKsp itself instead of half of it for a one-to-one salt
takes a cube root appropriate to a different salt stoichiometry
introduces a decade error when converting log solubility

questions.explanation: For a one-to-one salt s is the square root of Ksp, so negative log s is half of pKsp. Using pKsp directly ignores the square root, and a cube-root exponent belongs to a different salt stoichiometry.
questions.hint: Take the square root before converting to log solubility.

questions.stem: A 1 to 1 salt has Ksp = 1.35e-11. Find the value of negative log s, where s is the molar solubility in pure water?

options.misconception: takes a cube root appropriate to a different salt stoichiometry
introduces a decade error when converting log solubility
uses pKsp itself instead of half of it for a one-to-one salt

questions.explanation: For a one-to-one salt s is the square root of Ksp, so negative log s is half of pKsp. Using pKsp directly ignores the square root, and a cube-root exponent belongs to a different salt stoichiometry.
questions.hint: Take the square root before converting to log solubility.
